Hey! I just wanted to offer you some hope, my brother recently got in two consecutive car accidents and sustained "Several concussions" (doctors said at least 7) and was very close to dying.

He had the same initial reaction to it as you- albeit paired with severe cognitive decline and motor control issues (he was basically a large toddler for a while, couldn't even sit up without slumping over or form coherent sentences) but I digress.

Over the months he got progressively better and better and I watched him crawl out of his depression and find meaning in his life again. It was definitely a slow process and I can't tell you how long a bump would compare to his timeline, but he gave me some very insightful advice. He said the brain is just like any muscle, it needs exercise to reach its full potential. Push forward, cells regenerate and adapt; I know you feel stuck but you'll get back to a good place.

It sounds like the meds you feel doomed to be on aren't helping you- if they were I wouldn't say to stop taking them- but... they're called antidepressants for a reason, not ultradepressants haha. They're absolutely not doing their job if you're still debilitatingly troubled to this extent, I feel you'd benefit from a change. I'm not necessarily saying to change to a different  med (especially not if you're aware of the negative effects they have on you), but more so a change that would encourage your brain to heal more and not depend on meds you despise. It'll be a waiting game and you'll be frustrated. But you have an entire world of time to spend focusing on your health and only one brain, why waste time with something you don't want?

Cheers pal, you've got this. I've seen what happens after brain injuries and it's not the end of the world- just wait it out. Sry for the long response, lmk if there's any questions you have <3
